scope: Full investigation of every data element available from the Jeanologia laser machines and the legacy central database.

sources.note: 26 machines, key = machine id. Fields: name, ip (IP or NetBIOS name), share, db, enabled, transport. Machine 20 has transport=http_push and no ip. Now imported into the platform `machines` table and editable from the UI.

SQLite, 107 MB, 868,873 production rows from 2018-01 to 2026-09 across 25 machines (machine 3 never collected). Tables: production, machine_performance, machine_downtime, machine_connectivity, collector_status. Only 8 of the 17 available stats.db columns were being collected.
One per machine. Table `production` with 17 columns, identical schema on all 20 machines reachable during the investigation. This is the primary production source.

NEVER COLLECTED BEFORE. ~1.3 million rows across the fleet. Tables: markingAlarms (768k), laserErrorsHistory (262k), errorrecord (115k), genericErrorsWarnings (101k), operationErrors (69k), headErrors (8.7k), headHCM (3.9k scan-head calibrations), maintenance.
NEVER COLLECTED BEFORE. Model, serial number, laser count, mannequins, camera, duty cycle limit, measured laser power (whiteLevelParams), device connections, column/motor configuration.
NEVER COLLECTED BEFORE. Activation code history with credit added and the balance recorded at activation time. Relevant to production continuity: a machine stops when rental credit is exhausted.

diodeBoardParameters (34 presets: mark speed, jump speed, frequency, duty cycle, laser gains, correction file), machine (pulse widths, quality factors, head-temperature enable). Slow-moving; captured as an identity snapshot.

Tables garments, machinealarms, machineerrors, machinestates, maintenance, measures — empty on every machine inspected. This is Jeanologia's own cloud buffer; if it is ever enabled it becomes a second, richer state feed (machine states and measures per garment). Worth re-checking after any eMark upgrade.
Gain per machine type and colour, FPA pixel maps. Reference data for print-quality analysis; not time series.
Not a readable SQLite file (encrypted by the vendor). Excluded.
Table/primary-key manifest used by the vendor's reinstall tool. No operational value.

fleet.operating_pattern: 24/7, three shifts; Friday is the low day (Egypt weekend)
known_data_quality_issues: 331 job records carry impossible timestamps (2027 and 2041) caused by machine clock drift, mostly on machines 5, 6 and 21. The platform flags these as `suspect=1`, excludes them from every KPI, and raises a data_quality alert.

~3,900 job records have an empty end_date. Some are jobs still running (used for live state); the rest are aborted jobs. The collector re-reads a trailing window of source rows every cycle so late end_date updates are captured.
eMarkVersion is 0 or NULL on rows written before 2021; treated as unknown.
Compact machines report copies >> units (multiple marks per garment); units is the correct production count, copies is the mark count.

fields.meaning: Machine-local job sequence number
Job start time on the machine clock
fields.alert: clock drift, machine stopped, excessive idle
fields.maintenance: correlates alarms with production
fields.productivity: gap to the previous job = idle/downtime

fields.meaning: Job finish time; empty while the job is still running
fields.alert: open job older than the downtime threshold
fields.maintenance: abnormally long cycles precede faults

fields.meaning: Design file marked, e.g. 8307-244-800-BLACK-36.jean5. Parsed into style, size and colour.
fields.kpi: output by style/size/colour, cycle time per design
fields.forecast: expected cycle time for a planned order
fields.maintenance: designs that consistently trigger alarms
fields.productivity: best-vs-average cycle time per design = recoverable seconds

fields.meaning: Number of marks executed in the job
fields.maintenance: laser duty accumulation

fields.meaning: Garments produced — the production count of record
fields.kpi: units/hour, units/shift, target achievement, OEE performance
fields.alert: production drop vs baseline, target risk

fields.meaning: Total laser-on time for the job
fields.kpi: laser duty = laser-on / job wall time
fields.forecast: irreducible processing time for capacity models
fields.maintenance: cumulative laser hours -> source degradation
fields.productivity: separates unavoidable marking time from recoverable handling time

fields.meaning: Machine login active when the job ran (operator or role account)
fields.alert: unexpected admin login on a production machine
fields.maintenance: who was present when a fault occurred
fields.productivity: operator comparison, training targets, shift handover analysis

fields.meaning: Alarm counter for laser 1 during the job
fields.maintenance: primary per-job fault signal for laser 1

fields.meaning: Alarm counter for laser 2 (twin-head machines)
fields.alert: asymmetry between alarm1 and alarm2 isolates the faulty head
fields.maintenance: identifies which laser head is degrading

fields.meaning: Whether the design optimizer was applied to the job
fields.kpi: cycle time with vs without optimizer
fields.productivity: quantifies the time saved by optimised designs

fields.meaning: Peak galvanometer scanner temperature during the job
fields.forecast: temperature trend per day predicts scanner failure
fields.maintenance: leading indicator of scan-head degradation and cooling problems

fields.meaning: Peak servo/driver temperature during the job
fields.maintenance: cooling and drive-electronics health

fields.meaning: Machine's own rolling average time for the design
fields.alert: deviation from the machine's own average

fields.meaning: eMark software version that produced the record
fields.maintenance: correlate fault patterns with software versions

fields.meaning: Marking-process alarms: shutter not opened, no shapes to mark, nitrogen, water, interlock, scanhead stop, marking position error
fields.maintenance: the single richest fault source — 768k records fleet-wide

fields.meaning: Laser-source faults: water flow low/below limit, external interlock, RF temperature high, VSWR, DC voltage low, laser head fault
fields.forecast: water-flow and VSWR trends predict chiller and RF failures
fields.maintenance: the core predictive-maintenance signal for the laser source; serialnumber identifies the physical source

fields.meaning: Scan-head faults, operator-action errors, and legacy system errors (errorrecord uses the YYYYMMDD::HHMMSS::mmm format, normalised on ingest)
fields.alert: head errors are treated as warnings by default
fields.maintenance: head errors localise faults to the scanner

fields.meaning: Machine-PC level events: 'Cloud disconnected', 'Disk space usage is NN%'
fields.alert: disk space warnings — a full disk stops data collection
fields.forecast: disk growth rate predicts when the machine PC will fill up
fields.maintenance: IT maintenance backlog

fields.meaning: Scan-head calibration measurement: galvo drive currents, hysteresis and gain slope per axis, recorded at each calibration
fields.alert: head_drift when the gain slope moves more than the threshold from its own history
fields.forecast: drift trajectory predicts when the scanner needs service
fields.maintenance: THE definitive predictive indicator for scan-head wear — previously unused
fields.productivity: a drifting head degrades mark quality before it fails

fields.field: name, machineType, nlasers, nmannequins, hasCamera, dutyMax, has40ixLaser, hasColumns, hasLengthSensor
fields.meaning: Which machine model this unit is configured as, and its hardware capability set
fields.kpi: normalise KPIs by model — a Compact is not comparable to a Twin
fields.maintenance: spare-part and service planning; dutyMax is the rated duty-cycle ceiling

fields.meaning: Machine serial number and the mechanical handling times the machine expects
fields.maintenance: asset identification for service records and warranty
fields.productivity: expected handling time is the theoretical floor for the performance model

fields.meaning: Measured laser output power at the last white-level calibration
fields.alert: measured power falling below the rated value
fields.forecast: power-decay curve predicts end of laser-source life
fields.maintenance: direct laser-source degradation measurement
fields.productivity: lower power means longer marking time for the same result

fields.field: device, type, comport, ipAddress, ipPort, timeout
fields.meaning: Peripheral wiring: lasers, columns, conveyor, chiller sensor, water-quality sensor, robot, RTC scan controller
fields.maintenance: documents which sensors exist per machine and where they are attached

fields.field: id, time, previous, added, rented, status
fields.meaning: Laser licence/rental credit events. `added` is credit granted (commonly 921,600), `previous` is the balance recorded when the code was applied, `time` is an epoch-milliseconds timestamp.
fields.alert: laser_credit_low — a machine stops producing when rental credit runs out
fields.forecast: burn rate against the balance predicts the next activation date
fields.maintenance: commercial/contract maintenance planning
fields.productivity: an unplanned credit expiry is a full production stop

fields.field: markSpeed, jumpSpeed, frequency, dutyCycle, laserGainL1/L2, powerFactor, correctionFile
fields.meaning: Optical and laser driver parameters per preset
fields.alert: parameter changed outside a service window
fields.maintenance: records the exact optical setup for a machine; differences between identical machines explain performance gaps
fields.productivity: mark/jump speed directly sets achievable cycle time

fields.meaning: end_date - init_date, the job's wall-clock duration
fields.maintenance: cycle-time creep is an early wear signal
fields.productivity: the denominator of every throughput metric

fields.meaning: laser_ms/1000 divided by elapsed_seconds — the share of the job the laser was actually marking
fields.productivity: the clearest measure of handling loss; fleet average is about 0.6, best machines reach 0.8

fields.meaning: Shift name and shift-adjusted business date (a night shift is credited to the day it started)
fields.maintenance: which shift generates the most faults

fields.meaning: 1 when the source timestamp is impossible (machine clock drift)
fields.maintenance: flags machines whose clock needs correcting

fields.meaning: PRODUCING / IDLE / STOPPED / ALARM / MAINTENANCE / OFFLINE / DISABLED and CONNECTED / SLOW / DISCONNECTED / NOT_RESPONDING
fields.maintenance: downtime attribution

not_yet_available: Reject / rework counts. The machines do not record quality outcomes, so the platform reports a clearly-labelled quality PROXY (jobs completed without an alarm) rather than a true OEE quality factor. Switch it off in Settings if you prefer a two-factor OEE, or feed real reject counts in later.
Energy consumption. No electrical metering is exposed by eMark. Laser-on time is the best available proxy and is already collected; a clamp meter or PLC feed would make true energy KPIs possible.
Planned maintenance schedule. error.db has a `maintenance` table but it is empty on every machine, so maintenance windows are set in the platform (machine status = maintenance) instead.
Order / work-order numbers. Jobs carry a design name only. Style, size and colour are parsed from the design filename; a link to the ERP order would allow order-level tracking.
cloudBuffer.db machine states and per-garment measures are empty today. If Jeanologia's cloud connector is enabled they become a second, higher-resolution state feed worth collecting.
